items.title: Flood victim count at PPS records slight increase; Royal Malaysian Navy sends 100 personnel to Pangkor
items.summary: In a statement, the Perak State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said 100 victims from 29 families were housed at the PPS at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Matang Gelugor, up from 90 victims from 27 families recorded at 4pm. The centre was opened to accommodate residents affected by flooding in Kampung Matang Pasir and Kampung Matang Gelugor. Meanwhile, 56 victims from 21 families remain at the PPS at SK Matang following a storm that affected residents in Kampung Changkat Baru Matang, Kampung Teluk Kertam, Kampung Melawati and Kampung Hujung Matang.

items.title: Ringgit opens mostly higher as GDP growth beats forecasts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened mostly higher against a basket of major currencies on Monday after Malaysia's advance estimate of third-quarter 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth came in stronger than expected at 5.3 per cent. Against the US dollar, the ringgit was little changed, quoted at 4.0790/0855 at 8 am compared with Friday's close of 4.0795/0835. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said stronger-than-expected economic growth could reinforce expectations of a potential normalisation of monetary policy.

items.title: RM1bil impairment unlikely to affect Public Bank's capital-return plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Public Bank Bhd's RM1 billion goodwill impairment at its Hong Kong operations is unlikely to have a material direct impact on its RM3.5 billion capital-return plan, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. The bank recently announced a full goodwill impairment of HK$1.96 billion (RM1 billion) at its 73.23 per cent-owned Hong Kong subsidiary, Public Financial Holdings Ltd, following an impairment assessment. Public Bank said the non-cash charge could reduce its financial year 2026 (FY26) consolidated earnings per share and net assets per share by four sen each.

items.title: Lawmakers to address M40 aid, Madani allocations and Tourism Compliance Focus Zone effectiveness in Dewan Rakyat today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Aid for M40 households, allocations for the Madani school and Kampung Angkat programmes, and the effectiveness of the Tourism Compliance Focus Zone (ZTPP) programme are among the issues scheduled to be raised at the Dewan Rakyat sitting today. According to the Order Paper on the Parliament website, Datuk Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah) will ask the Finance Minister to explain measures to help M40 households no longer eligible for targeted aid but affected by rising living costs, including a mechanism to reassess eligibility based on current income and expenditure. Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman anak Begri (GPS-Betong) will ask the Finance Minister to explain the detailed breakdown of the RM50 million and RM200 million spent on the Madani School and Kampung Angkat programmes, to ensure transparency over the financial impact and the actual number of beneficiaries under the People's Housing Programme (PPR).

items.title: Mount Kinabalu records 239 emergency cases involving hikers since 2022
items.summary: Sabah Fire and Rescue Department director Mohd Pisar Aziz said the figure highlights the need for continuous readiness among rescue teams at the state's iconic mountain, which attracts both domestic and international climbers. He said that despite its beauty and appeal, Mount Kinabalu poses high safety risks, with every incident demanding thorough assessment, appropriate action, and effective coordination among all parties involved. "Therefore, the department remains committed to providing emergency assistance and conducting search and rescue operations within the department's jurisdiction, competency, and capabilities," he said.

items.title: PM Anwar: Malaysia prepared to assist Indonesia in tackling forest fires
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Malaysia remains prepared to extend assistance to Indonesia in addressing forest and land fires that have resulted in transboundary haze. Furthermore, Malaysia has proposed a cooperation mechanism at the Asean level to strengthen joint action in tackling this issue. “We have proposed a cooperation mechanism at the Asean level to strengthen coordination, preparedness, and collective action in dealing with transboundary haze,” he also said.

items.title: Haze: 27 areas record unhealthy API readings, Johan Setia highest at 173
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings were recorded in 27 areas nationwide as of 8am today, with Johan Setia in Selangor logging the highest level at 173. Nilai in Negri Sembilan followed at 169, while Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded 168. In Negri Sembilan, Seremban recorded 165 and Port Dickson 153.

items.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu, warns Israel against choosing rival in tight election
items.summary: JERUSALEM: US President Donald Trump endorsed on Sunday his ally Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel's close-fought parliamentary election on Oct 27, providing a boost to the veteran prime minister's bid to win a new mandate. The endorsement comes less than two weeks before Israel's first vote since the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack, which opposition politicians have accused Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for after allegedly ignoring warnings. Trump and Netanyahu, who polls show is in a tight election race, have worked closely together on Israel's multi-front wars after the Hamas-led attack, including bombarding Iran, and the endorsement could be a boon to his re-election campaign.

items.title: Oil slips as Trump's sanction waiver may lead to more Russian fuel supplies
items.summary: Brent crude futures fell US$1.43, or 1.3 per cent, to US$108.43 a barrel by 2340 GMT after settling at its highest since May 19 on Friday. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$100.88 a barrel, down 53 cents, or 0.52 per cent. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said these US actions will hurt Ukraine.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pas machinery mobilised, PN confident of defeating PH
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) is confident of defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) in next month's Melaka state election. The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election, with nomination day scheduled for Oct 31. Melaka has 28 state seats.

items.title: M40 aid, Madani school funding among issues in Dewan Rakyat today
items.summary: According to the Order Paper on the Parliament website, Datuk Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah) will ask the finance minister about measures to assist M40 households no longer eligible for targeted aid but affected by the rising cost of living. Hassan Saad (PN-Baling) will ask the domestic trade and cost of living minister for performance indicators used to evaluate the ZTPP programme's effectiveness in curbing price-gouging complaints. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, presented the 2027 Budget on Oct 9.

items.title: Nikkei slides on US tech selloff, oil-driven rate fears
items.summary: The benchmark Nikkei 225 fell 2.05 per cent to 63,984.45 in early trading. The broader Topix slipped 1.22 per cent to 4,016.34. The largest losers were Taiyo Yuden, down 7.42 per cent, followed by Sumitomo Electric Ind., 5.96 per cent lower, and Sumco, which lost 5.88 per cent.

items.title: Hazy Monday dawns, 26 stations across Kuala Lumpur, Johor, Sarawak record poor air
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — Malaysia woke up to another a hazy Monday morning with air quality readings showing 26 monitoring stations across the country recording unhealthy levels at 6am. According to the Department of Environment (DOE), stations in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, Johor and Sarawak were among those affected. The overall Air Pollutant Index (API) stood at 26 stations in the unhealthy range, while 39 stations recorded moderate readings and only three were classified as good.

items.title: Bomb threat forces Tel Aviv-Vienna flight to divert to Bulgaria
items.summary: SOFIA: A bomb threat against an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna on Sunday forced the plane to divert to Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian authorities and the airline. The Austrian Airlines crew decided to make an emergency landing in Sofia after reportedly receiving a bomb threat as they neared Romania, Bulgaria's transport ministry said in a statement, adding that the passengers were evacuated from the aircraft after landing. The Bulgarian air force scrambled a MiG-29 fighter jet to escort the airliner as part of established procedures, the transport ministry said.

items.title: Lorry driver held after container crushes car, killing father and daughter
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A 49-year-old lorry driver has been detained after a container fell onto a car, killing a father and daughter near Sepanggar Port yesterday. Kota Kinabalu police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said preliminary investigations found that the Hino container lorry had stopped by the roadside to load a container onto its trailer. He said the lorry driver was loading the container when it suddenly became unstable and fell to the right, crushing the victims' car as it travelled along the right lane towards Sepanggar Port.

items.title: Trump defends Russia sanctions waiver, accuses Zelenskyy of prolonging war
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday defended his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, while once again accusing Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. The remarks come after Trump signed an executive order late Friday waiving broad new sanctions mandated by legislation named for the late US senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Ukraine's defence. Trump said.

items.title: Frail Indonesian markets reel after MSCI shock warning
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Indonesian markets face a tense start on Monday after a warning from MSCI over possible expulsion from some of its indexes next year rattled already fragile investor sentiment and sparked a furious selloff in the world's worst-performing stock market. Jakarta stocks sank 11.6 per cent on Friday, the benchmark's biggest one-day drop in nearly three decades, taking year-to-date losses to 40 per cent, after MSCI said it was considering shifting Indonesia to "standalone" status from its current "emerging markets" mantle. Goldman Sachs estimates a full MSCI removal could trigger US$5.6 billion of passive outflows.

items.title: Indonesia Stock Exchange cuts its lower auto-rejection limit to 7pct from 15pct
items.summary: JAKARTA: The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Monday it cut its lower auto-rejection limit to seven per cent from 15 per cent, effective immediately and to be reassessed periodically. "This adjustment is aimed at giving investors an opportunity to evaluate and digest available information, helping them make better investment decisions based on Indonesia's economic fundamentals," the exchange said in a statement. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: MBSB explores acquisitions to fuel next growth phase
items.summary: Chairman Datuk Wan Kamaruzaman Wan Ahmad said the group is considering acquiring financial institutions or selected assets from other industry players as part of its longer-term growth strategy. Wan Kamaruzaman said MBSB is particularly interested in exploring mortgage portfolios, while a credit card business could be established organically or acquired from an existing operator. Takaful operations are another potential area of expansion, said Wan Kamaruzaman.

items.title: Can Gamuda meet FY27 earnings projections?
items.summary: In fact, in the financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY26) alone, the construction group has secured RM36 billion worth of new contracts. Between then and October 16, Gamuda's share price increased by 28.7 per cent to close at RM4.78 per share. In FY21, Gamuda's net profit margins was 17.97 per cent, when the group earned RM632.19 million out of RM3.52 billion revenue.

items.title: France's debt reckoning: The price of sovereignty
items.summary: France's next political contest will also be a test of fiscal credibility. France has not defaulted. France's difficulties predate Le Pen's programme.

items.title: Lindung 24 Jam offers income support, rehab after accidents
items.summary: Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed said its Lindung 24 Jam scheme provides eligible workers with access to treatment and rehabilitation following accidents occurring outside working hours. Under its "Care Beyond Compensation" approach, eligible workers can receive rehabilitation equipment and injury-related implants, as well as physical rehabilitation at Perkeso's rehabilitation centres. "Lindung 24 Jam helps ease this burden through the Temporary Disablement Benefit, which replaces income during approved medical leave.

items.title: PN logo use, Negri crisis among key court cases this week
items.summary: The application is among four high-profile court cases scheduled for this week, including two related to the Negri Sembilan crisis and a defamation-related contempt action. The High Court had also refused to stay the contempt proceedings pending their appeal, prompting them to seek a stay from the Court of Appeal. On July 29, the appellate court granted an interim stay barring the Seremban High Court from proceeding with the contempt case.

items.title: 38,000 rejected claims expose gap in workers' safety net
items.summary: Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the figure, recorded between 2015 and 2025, exposed a significant gap in social protection for workers injured outside working hours, particularly those without private insurance or takaful coverage. Citing Bank Negara Malaysia data, he said personal insurance or takaful ownership among B40 workers remained low, at between four and 30 per cent, compared with 88 per cent among higher-income urban workers. Khairul Firdaus said the low contribution could provide crucial support to workers who suffered serious injuries or disabilities from accidents outside working hours.

items.title: Melaka polls: Seat deals remain the wild card [WATCH]
items.summary: But despite preparations being well underway, uncertainty over political cooperation and seat negotiations means the final electoral landscape may not be clear until nomination day. BN and Pas have indicated that their candidate lists are ready, while PH has finalised seat allocations among its components, PKR, DAP and Amanah. Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said early candidate preparations demonstrated organisational readiness and allowed parties to assess candidates' acceptance among voters.

items.title: 'Our job is to be right, not popular,' says Chief Justice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The judiciary must earn public confidence through integrity, transparency and accountability rather than chase popularity. Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh said that social media had intensified scrutiny of court decisions, with judgments often condemned or praised before the public had read the legal reasoning behind them. Wan Ahmad Farid said the distinction between public confidence, which the judiciary must earn, and public approval, which it must not pursue, was central to preserving judicial independence.

items.title: Lindung 24 Jam: Protection that goes beyond the workplace
items.summary: Without personal medical insurance, Ridhuan had to rely on his company's medical coverage, as he was not eligible for Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) protection because the accident occurred outside working hours. Although his company provided medical coverage, it wasn't enough for the treatment. OFF-HOUR PROTECTION Ridhuan said the introduction of Perkeso's Non-Employment Injury Scheme, also known as Lindung 24 Jam, would provide workers with protection against accidents outside working hours.

items.title: Ex-Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman faces 'high legal hurdle' in bid to block MACC asset notice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Yayasan Bank Rakyat (YBR) chairman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin's bid to block an asset declaration notice from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) faces a high legal hurdle. Bar Council Criminal Law Committee chairman Vivekananda Sukumaran said courts generally decline to interfere with MACC's investigative powers, while legislation imposed further restrictions on injunctions against public authorities. They also want an injunction preventing MACC from issuing or serving asset declaration notices against them.

items.title: Budget 2027: Don’t miss these tax reliefs when you file your taxes next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Before you file your next income tax return, remember to lookout for existing and new tax reliefs. If you do not already know, taxpayers can even make claims for artificial intelligence (AI) subscriptions — a first for Malaysia’s individual tax reliefs — alongside existing reliefs for education, healthcare and social security contributions. Existing tax reliefs and what will change Education and skills training The existing education fee relief of up to RM7,000 will be expanded to cover qualifying formal education in any field.

items.title: 'France is burning': Trump blames immigration for unrest, urges border crackdown
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. "France is burning! Trump's post comes after similar comments made by Vice President JD Vance on Saturday.

items.title: Malaysian honoured for boosting Japan ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian educator and cultural exchange advocate Gary Tang has received the Japanese Foreign Minister's Commendation for helping to strengthen Malaysia-Japan relations. Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki said Tang was one of two Malaysians selected this year among 159 individuals and 67 groups honoured worldwide. He said Tang had played a pivotal role in promoting study opportunities in Japan among Malaysian youth since becoming president of the Japan Graduates' Association of Malaysia (Jagam) in 2018.

items.title: France protests descend into looting as 1,500 businesses suffer damage
items.summary: PARIS: French police battled protesters and looters for a second day Sunday as the country reeled from the violent chaos left by a day of cost-of-living demonstrations in which 2,000 people were arrested nationwide. AFP journalists said several hundred people gathered in the Republique square in the capital following social media calls for a gathering that authorities said had not been approved. [[nid:1558535]] The Paris police prefecture said security forces moved in when "faced with the initial signs of tension."

items.title: E-Commerce Bill set for first parliamentary sitting next year
items.summary: KUANTAN: The E-Commerce Bill, aimed at strengthening accountability among online platforms and sellers, will be tabled at the first parliamentary sitting next year. Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the draft was being refined. In Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia Retail Chain Association president Datuk Liew Bin said the bill was crucial to fostering a healthy digital economy.

items.title: MediAsas plan to offer financial, health safety net to Malaysia's M40: Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The MediAsas Plan scheme, set to launch in January 2027, will provide a financial and healthcare safety net for Malaysia's middle-income group (M40), who are currently facing medical inflation. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the plan would provide protection to the M40 group through transparent cost control without hidden or excessive charges. Earlier, the Finance Ministry announced that MediAsas, which provides protection for individuals up to 85 years of age, will be offered as a separate (standalone) medical insurance and takaful protection plan that includes two product options, namely MediAsas Teras (standard plan) and MediAsas Flexi (standard-plus plan).

items.title: Macron vows crackdown as France protests leave 2,400 arrested, nearly 1,000 police injured
items.summary: PARIS: President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday slammed the "unbridled" violence that erupted in cost-of-living protests across France, as police battled protesters and looters in new clashes in Paris. Nearly 2,400 people were arrested Saturday in unrest that represented some of the worst urban violence in France in years, with almost 1,000 police and gendarmes injured, seven seriously, the interior ministry said. In an address to the nation, Macron said local authorities would be able to ban – "if necessary" – certain rallies in coming days.

items.title: EIS benefits rise to RM25,000 as Socso steps up support for jobseekers
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 18 — The Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Employment Insurance System (EIS) helps workers who have lost their jobs rebuild their livelihoods through financial assistance, career guidance and support in securing new employment. Perkeso deputy chief executive (Operations) Azirruan Arifin said 117,733 jobseekers had secured employment across various sectors between January and August 14 this year through the organisation’s employment support services. He said Perkeso provided financial and training support to help jobseekers overcome these challenges and improve their chances of securing employment.

items.title: Old Socso contributions open door to life-changing stroke rehabilitation
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — For five years, a wheelchair was Salinah Osman’s constant companion, confining the once-active massage therapist to a life far removed from the independence she had enjoyed before suffering a second stroke in 2021. Her breakthrough came when she learnt about the rehabilitation benefits available to contributors of the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) who had suffered strokes, prompting her to submit an application. In April, Salinah was offered an intensive rehabilitation programme at the Sultan Nazrin Shah Perkeso Rehabilitation Centre in Meru here, with the cost fully covered by Perkeso.

items.title: Flood relief centres shut in Penang, Pahang and Kedah, Perak keeps two open
items.summary: In PAHANG, two PPS in Raub housing 26 evacuees from 11 families were also closed at 1pm today. However, the Perak State Disaster Management Committee secretariat said two PPS remained in operation as of 4pm, at SK Matang Gelugor and SK Matang. The floods hit Kampung Matang Pasir and Kampung Matang Gelugor, while the storm also struck Kampung Changkat Baru Matang, Kampung Teluk Kertam, Kampung Melawati and Kampung Hujung Matang.

items.title: Public Service Dept says Hybrid Workday policy can be used to adapt to haze conditions
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 18 — Department heads in the public service sector can leverage the Hybrid Workday (HBH) Policy to adapt to haze conditions in their respective states. Public Service Department (PSD) director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said that department heads may employ appropriate methods under the HBH framework to ensure that work deliverables or Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for every civil servant are met. Also present was the Terengganu Federal Development Department director Datuk Abdul Kahar Abdul Latif.

items.title: Masidi: RM18.7b Sabah allocation covers civil service salaries, not just projects
items.summary: KUDAT, Oct 18 — The RM18.7 billion allocated to Sabah under Budget 2027 is not solely for development projects, but also covers the operating costs of federal ministries and departments in the state, Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun said. He said a large portion of the allocation will cover operating expenses, including salaries for about 120,000 federal civil servants working in Sabah. We need to understand that the allocation also covers the operating costs of federal ministries and departments operating in Sabah.

items.title: Melaka election to see wider use of OCR‑VA system, Election Commission confident after MCMC tests
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Election Commission (EC) have conducted internet connectivity checks at polling centres to test the Optical Character Recognition-Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system ahead of the Melaka state election, which will take place next month. State Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications Committee chairman Datuk Fairul Nizam Roslan said one polling centre, Dewan Penyayang at the Lesung Batu Welfare Complex, was found to be unsuitable for the OCR-VA system due to unsatisfactory internet connectivity. Fairul Nizam said MCMC had also submitted a full report to the EC on internet connectivity at the polling centres to facilitate arrangements on election day.

items.title: Singer Yusuf Islam visits grieving Dr Mahathir, offers prayers for late Tun Dr Hasmah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — British singer songwriter Yusuf Islam, better known as Cat Stevens, paid a visit to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today, following the recent passing of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali. In a Facebook post, Yusuf said he read Al-Fatihah with Dr Mahathir, noting that the couple had been married for 70 years. The gesture drew warm responses from admirers, many thanking the musician for consoling Dr Mahathir in his grief.

items.title: Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang and Penang schools resume Oct 19, masks encouraged
items.summary: In SELANGOR, the State Education Department (JPN) said that outdoor activities are to be suspended, and students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks. School administrators are required to continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and pay special attention to high-risk students. In MELAKA, the State Education Department (JPN) said that school administrators must continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings provided by the Department of Environment (DOE) and pay special attention to high-risk students.

items.title: Perak shuts all hiking trails in forest reserves from Nov 2 to Jan 17 due to monsoon season
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — All hiking trails and recreational activities within permanent forest reserves (HSK) in Perak will be closed to the public from November 2 to January 17 next year due to the monsoon season. Perak Forestry director Datuk Mohd Basri Abdul Manaf said the directive took into account current risk assessments and the weather outlook report issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). “All hiking trails and recreational activities within Perak’s HSK, including jungle trekking, four-wheel driving and cycling, are prohibited during this period,” he said in a notice posted on the Perak Forestry Department’s official website.

items.title: Nationwide haze surge pushes API past 150 in 26 areas, Pasir Gudang worst at 182
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — A total of 26 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of this afternoon, with Pasir Gudang, Johor, recording the highest reading at 182. All three monitoring areas in Melaka also recorded unhealthy readings: Bukit Rambai (166), Melaka City (158) and Alor Gajah (157). A total of 41 areas recorded moderate API readings, while one area recorded a good reading.

items.title: Fahmi confirms Pakatan vetting complete, Melaka candidates to sign bond with RM10m penalty
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has completed vetting candidates who will contest the 16th Melaka state election, including checks with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said PH will announce its candidates on Oct 24, once the selection process is finalised. In the previous state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 state seats contested, while PH secured five.

items.title: Police open two probes into viral issue involving activist and Myanmar refugee community in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 18 — Police have opened two investigation papers following a viral issue involving a social media activist and the Myanmar refugee community in Kelantan, including a robbery case that led to the arrest of two local men. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the cases were being investigated under Sections 341 and 268, and Section 395 of the Penal Code. He said two local men had been arrested to assist in investigations into a robbery involving a member of the Rohingya refugee community.

items.title: Hajiji urges GRS parties to put Sabah first, warns against ego and power struggles
items.summary: KUDAT, Oct 18 — All component parties of Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) must prioritise the interests of Sabah and the coalition over personal or individual party interests, in order to strengthen the state’s bargaining power at the federal level, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. The Chief Minister of Sabah said the state’s political leverage in negotiations at the federal level must be anchored in the internal cohesion of GRS, rather than being undermined by power struggles for positions or political egos. Also present were GRS deputy chairmen Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, Tan Sri Anifah Aman, Tan Sri Liew Yun Fah, Datuk Ewon Benedick, and Datuk Chin Su Phin, as well as GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.

items.title: MCMC probes Threads content suspected of insulting Negeri Sembilan royal institution
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has launched an investigation into content uploaded on the social media platform Threads, suspected of containing insults against the royal institution of Negeri Sembilan. In a statement today, MCMC said the content in question touches on issues concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. As part of the investigation, MCMC recorded a statement from an individual at the Labu police station.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Najib’s house arrest conditions being finalised, but RM50m fine yet to be settled
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that the matter is being pursued following a letter from the Pardons Board secretariat, which allows the Malaysian Prisons Department to set conditions for the implementation of house arrest. “The Malaysian Prisons Department is in the final phase, currently drafting it. In the letter from the Pardons Board secretariat to the Malaysian Prisons Department, it is stated that the Malaysian Prisons Department can impose any conditions.

items.title: Fahmi condemns cyberbullying of UM student Ummi after she questioned Najib fine donations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has condemned the bullying and threats directed at Universiti Malaya (UM) student Ummi Umairah Bakhit following views she expressed at a forum. He also urged all victims of cyberbullying to immediately lodge reports with the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) immediately. Fahmi said users should not assume that online posts carried no consequences, including when accounts used were believed to be fake.

items.title: Kuching, Samarahan and Serian record unhealthy API readings as haze lingers over Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 18 — Kuching, Samarahan and Serian recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm today. According to the Natural Resource and Environment Board (NREB) website, Serian recorded the highest reading at 155, followed by Kuching 154 and Samarahan 148. Seventeen districts recorded moderate levels.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya and 10 states until 6pm
items.summary: In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the warning covers the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as selected areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kelantan, the affected areas are Jeli, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang, while in Terengganu, they are Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang. In Pahang, the affected areas are Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, they are Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Sepang, Kuala Langat and Kuala Selangor.

items.title: Pakatan finalises Melaka seat allocation but no deal yet with other parties, says PKR sec-gen
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has yet to reach any concrete agreement on possible political cooperation with other parties for the November 14 Melaka state election. Datuk Fuziah Salleh, who is Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) secretary-general, said, however, that seat-allocation negotiations among its three component parties — PKR, DAP and Amanah — had been finalised. She said PH was expected to contest more than 20 state seats, with nine allocated to PKR.

items.title: HRD Corp training grant applications surge after system reforms, says Ramanan
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 18 — The surge in Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) training grant applications reflects the positive impact of measures taken to streamline its implementation system, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan. It takes considerable time, and we thank the entire HRD Corp team for their dedication to carrying out these improvements,” he told reporters after attending the HRD Corp ‘Pocket Talk’ Roadshow: From Policy to the People here today. Also present was HRD Corp chief executive officer Datuk Shamir Aziz.

items.title: Hajiji recalls mother borrowing RM15 for exam fees as he vows poverty will not define Sabah children
items.summary: KUDAT, Oct 18 — Ensuring that poverty does not determine the fate of Sabah’s children or stand in the way of their progress has become a personal mission and commitment for Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Education is what can lift our children out of poverty. Driven by this commitment, he said he had ensured that the state government increased the allocation for the Sabah State Government Scholarship (BKNS) to RM155 million in 2026, up from RM55 million in 2021, to fund the education of students from underprivileged backgrounds.

items.title: Unesco status alone won’t save silat if youth turn away, says Perak MB
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (Unesco) recognition of silat as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity does not guarantee its survival if younger generations increasingly distance themselves from training, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said. “We may have a proud silat heritage, but if young people turn away from the training arena, fewer will truly master and appreciate the art,” he said. Saarani said Malaysia has more than 150 identified silat styles, with the martial art declared a National Heritage in 2009 before gaining Unesco recognition as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2019.

items.title: ‘We cannot sit back’: Malaysia offers aircraft to fight Indonesia forest fires despite dangerously poor visibility
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Malaysia cannot afford to stand by as raging forest fires in Indonesia send thick haze across the region, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today, as the country offered to deploy helicopters and water-bombing aircraft to help contain the blazes. But Mohamad warned that dangerously poor visibility, reportedly below 50m in affected areas, could hamper aerial firefighting operations and put pilots at risk. Thick smoke was also preventing aircraft from operating safely.

items.title: Anwar approves RM30m to resurface 600 roads in Perak, says Nga Kor Ming
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved a special allocation of RM30 million to resurface 600 roads in residential areas across Perak, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. “In conjunction with the Perak DAP Convention, I announced on behalf of the Prime Minister a special allocation of RM30 million for road resurfacing works in residential areas across the state. He said this while speaking at the 24th Perak DAP Annual Convention, officiated by DAP Secretary-General Anthony Loke here today.

items.title: E-Commerce Bill to be tabled next year to regulate online transactions, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 18 — The E-Commerce Bill will be tabled in Parliament at the first meeting next year to strengthen the regulation of online transactions, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh. Fuziah said the Retail Access Programme, which combines training and business matching, has helped 1,862 entrepreneurs from 2023 to October this year. She said the programme comprised 38 training series and 21 business matching series, involving 103 local brands and 552 stock-keeping units (SKUs).
